title: Soft Body Fish Swimming with Muscle Deformation
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with an interactive 3D soft-body fish swimming simulation using Three.js. The scene features a loaded GLB model representing the fish body, deformed in real-time by a spring-mass soft-body system simulating muscular contractions.

## Scene Setup
- Use Three.js r152+ via CDN with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls.
- Camera: PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 3, 10), lookAt (0, 0, 0).
- Lights: One DirectionalLight (white, intensity 1.2) at (5, 10, 7), one AmbientLight (0x4488cc, 0.4) for underwater feel.
- Background: Set renderer clear color to 0x0a2a4a (deep ocean blue).
- Add a large semi-transparent plane at y=-3 with color 0x1a3a5a as the ocean floor.
- Load the model 'PrimaryIonDrive.glb' using GLTFLoader. Once loaded, scale it to fit within a bounding sphere of radius ~1.5 and center it at origin. This mesh acts as the fish body visual.

## Soft Body Spine System
- Create a spine of 12 mass-point nodes along the fish's local Z-axis (head at index 0, tail at index 11), evenly spaced.
- Each node has: position (vec3), velocity (vec3), mass (0.1 for head, 0.05 for body nodes).
- Connect adjacent nodes with spring constraints: rest length = spacing between nodes, stiffness k=15.0, damping d=0.5.
- The head node (index 0) is the driver node and is NOT free — it follows a swimming path.

## Muscle Deformation
- Implement a sinusoidal muscle wave that propagates from head to tail: lateral offset = amplitude * sin(frequency * time - phaseShift * nodeIndex).
- Default amplitude: 0.3, frequency: 3.0, phaseShift: 0.8 per node.
- Apply this lateral offset as a force on each spine node in the local X-axis direction.
- After physics integration (semi-implicit Euler, dt capped at 1/60), deform the loaded GLB mesh vertices: each vertex is influenced by the nearest 2 spine nodes (weighted by inverse distance) to compute its displaced position.
- Store original vertex positions on first frame for reference.

## Swimming Path
- The head node follows a figure-eight (lemniscate) path in the XZ plane: x = 4*cos(t*0.3), z = 4*sin(t*0.3)*cos(t*0.3), y = 0.
- The fish body should orient (lookAt) toward its velocity direction with smooth interpolation (slerp, factor 0.05).

## User Interactions
- Keyboard 'ArrowUp': Increase swim speed multiplier by 0.2 (max 3.0).
- Keyboard 'ArrowDown': Decrease swim speed multiplier by 0.2 (min 0.2).
- Keyboard 'M': Toggle muscle deformation on/off. When off, amplitude=0 and spine nodes stay rigid along the forward axis.
- Keyboard 'Space': Toggle pause/resume of the entire simulation.
- Click on the fish mesh (raycasting): Apply a lateral impulse of magnitude 2.0 to all spine nodes (simulating a startle reflex), decaying over 0.5 seconds.
- DOM button 'Reset' (id='resetBtn'): Reset fish to initial position, speed=1.0, muscle on, unpaused.
- DOM button 'Toggle Trail' (id='trailBtn'): Toggle a trailing particle effect behind the tail node (index 11). Use a BufferGeometry point cloud of up to 200 points.

## HUD / UI
- Overlay div (id='hud') at top-left showing: Speed: X.X | Muscle: ON/OFF | Paused: YES/NO | Spine Energy: X.XX | Trail: ON/OFF.
- 'resetBtn' and 'trailBtn' as styled buttons at bottom-center.

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ with:
- modelLoaded: boolean, true once GLB is loaded.
- spineNodes: array of 12 objects each with {x, y, z, vx, vy, vz}.
- speedMultiplier: number (current swim speed multiplier).
- muscleActive: boolean.
- paused: boolean.
- amplitude: number (current muscle amplitude).
- frequency: number.
- headPosition: {x, y, z} of node 0.
- tailPosition: {x, y, z} of node 11.
- spineKineticEnergy: number (sum of 0.5*m*v^2 for all nodes).
- trailActive: boolean.
- trailPointCount: number (current number of trail points rendered).
- startleActive: boolean (true while startle impulse is decaying).
- elapsedTime: number (simulation time in seconds).
- meshVertexCount: number (vertex count of loaded mesh).
- frameCount: number.

Update __3D_STATE__ every frame in the animation loop.
physics_constraints: Spring-mass system with semi-implicit Euler integration. Springs: k=15, d=0.5. Muscle wave is sinusoidal propagation head-to-tail. Kinetic energy must remain finite and NaN-free. Spine node positions must stay within a reasonable bounding box (±10 units from origin). Speed multiplier clamped [0.2, 3.0]. Startle impulse decays exponentially over 0.5s.
